text: In the same forest lived a boy named Ekalavya.
He dreamed of learning archery from Guru Drona.
But Drona taught only princes. He sent the boy away.
Ekalavya did not give up.
Deep in the forest, he shaped a statue of Drona from clay.
Every day, he bowed to it, and practised.
Dawn after dawn. Season after season.
One day, a dog barked at him.
In a blink, seven arrows closed its mouth, without a single wound.
Drona and Arjuna were amazed.
Who is your teacher?
You are, Guru-ji.
Drona asked for his fee: the boy’s right thumb.
Ekalavya gave it, without a moment’s doubt.
He lost his thumb, but his devotion became immortal.
When the will is true, you will find a way to learn.
Long ago, two boys studied together: Krishna and Sudama.
They shared everything, and promised to stay friends forever.
Years passed. Krishna became the king of Dwarka.
Sudama remained poor.
His wife said, Go and see your friend.
But Sudama had nothing to give, only a handful of flattened rice.
At the golden palace, he stood ashamed.
Then Krishna saw him, and ran to the gate, barefoot.
He embraced his old friend, and washed his tired feet.
Sudama hid his little bundle.
But Krishna took it, and ate the rice with joy.
The finest gift I have ever received.
Sudama went home without asking for anything.
And found his hut had become a palace.
A true friend does not see what you bring,
only who you are.
By a river stood a jamun tree, home to a clever monkey.
Every day, he shared its sweet fruit with a crocodile.
They became good friends.
But the crocodile’s wife said, If the fruit is so sweet…
…imagine how sweet the monkey’s heart must be!
So the crocodile invited the monkey home, on his back.
In the middle of the river, he said, My wife wants your heart.
The monkey was afraid. But he stayed calm.
Oh, friend! I left my heart in the tree.
Take me back, and I will bring it.
The foolish crocodile swam back.
The monkey leapt to the top of the tree, and never came down.
When danger comes, panic is your enemy.
A calm mind will always find a way.
Five stories from ancient India.
Five lessons for every life.
Story one. Focus.
Story two. Dedication.
Story three. What truly matters.
Story four. Friendship.
Story five. Presence of mind.
Focus. Dedication. Love. Friendship. A calm mind.
Which lesson will you carry with you?

Long ago, on Mount Kailash,
a golden fruit fell from the heavens.
The fruit of all wisdom.
But it could not be shared.
And Shiva had two sons.
Kartikeya, the swift,
and Ganesha, the wise.
Whoever circles the whole world
three times first,
wins the fruit.
Kartikeya leapt onto his peacock
and was gone in a flash.
Ganesha looked at his little mouse.
And smiled.
Over oceans.
Over mountains.
Across every land.
Ganesha simply walked around his parents.
Once.
Twice.
Three times.
You are my whole world.
And the fruit was his.
When Kartikeya returned, the race was already won.
That is why they say,
the world is not out there.
It is the ones who made you.
